edits.value_json: The current graph 学 is arranged ⿳⺍冖子: ⺍ and 冖 form an upper assembly above 子. This visible split does not settle how traditional 學 was first constructed. One account interprets oracle-bone forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Separate proposals describe associative forms involving 升 + 冖 or 林 + 冖; phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 升 or 冖 as the other element; a rare element read jù, described as hands or claws and assigned both sound and meaning roles; and a distinct proposal involving two 臼 (犹升) forms with 冖, with 臼 also described as a sound element. Another proposal says 子 was added in Western Zhou forms to mark a child learner. These are competing interpretations, not a settled reconstruction. The modern simplified shape does not establish the ancient structure.

A database search result reports 學 as a borrowed spelling for the different word 覺, “feel” or “perceive,” in Han slips. The cited context was not directly inspected, and the reason for this spelling is not established. This reported spelling loan is not a meaning that developed from “learning”.
